desc:
Migrating a native or hybrid app to Flutter moves your product into one codebase for iPhone and Android. Ecom Swift LLC plans the move, rebuilds your screens in Flutter and carries over your data and users, with test builds before any store update.

## What does it mean to migrate an app to Flutter?

Migrating to Flutter means rebuilding an existing app in Flutter and Dart while keeping what users already depend on: their accounts, their data, their purchases and the way the app behaves. The old app is the specification. The new app replaces it under the same store listing.

The source can be a native iOS app in Swift, a native Android app in Kotlin or Java, or an older cross-platform app built with another framework. Each has its own quirks, but the process is the same: list, map, rebuild, test and release.

## Why teams move to one codebase

Two native apps mean two sets of developers, two bug lists and two release schedules. Features arrive on one system weeks before the other, and small differences in behavior become support questions. An older hybrid app can bring different pain: slow screens, plugins no one maintains and a framework the team no longer wants.

A single Flutter codebase puts that work in one place. The same screen is written once, the same fix is applied once and the same test checks both platforms. That does not remove all platform work, since notifications, purchases and permissions still need care on each system, but it narrows it.

## How a migration affects your product and your costs

The main gain is maintenance. After the move, a change that used to cost two developers' time costs one. Feature parity stops being a project of its own. A smaller team can keep both platforms current.

The main risk is losing users along the way. Existing customers should update the app as usual and find their login, data and purchases intact. Migration done well makes that boring. Migration done carelessly can log people out, drop saved content or break subscriptions, which is why the data plan and the update path are tested before release.

## What a careful migration includes

- An inventory of every screen, feature, permission and background task in the current app.
- A decision on what to carry over, simplify or drop, agreed in writing.
- A data model map, so each stored field has a clear place in the new app.
- Connection to your existing API without forcing backend changes.
- Login carried over, so users do not need to register again.
- Push notifications ported, with tokens handled for both platforms.
- In-app purchases rebuilt for both stores, with restore purchases tested.
- A tested update path from the old app version to the new one.
- Test builds through TestFlight and Google Play internal testing.
- Native code bridges for features that Flutter plugins do not cover.

## How we carry out the move

We begin by using your current app and reading what we can of its code, then write the migration plan with the feature list. We rebuild in order of importance: the core flow first, then supporting screens. Because you can test builds early, you see real progress and can correct course.

Data is handled with the same care as screens. We map what the old app stores locally and on the server, move what must move and test with real upgrade scenarios, such as installing the old version, adding data, then updating to the new one. The Basic package delivers the plan and the first core screens. The Standard package produces a working Flutter version of the core product with data carried over. The Premium package completes a larger set of screens, purchases and store release support. We can also move gradually, running parts of the product in Flutter before the whole app is replaced, where your current app allows it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give us the current source code, design files and API documents you have.
- Keep the old app available until the new one is proven.
- Name the features your users depend on most.
- Test the update on a phone that has real data in the old app.
- Plan the release with a fallback if something unexpected appears.

**Avoid:**
- Rebuilding every legacy feature without asking whether people use it.
- Changing the backend and the app at the same time.
- Releasing without testing the upgrade from the old version.
- Forgetting subscribers, who need their access preserved.
- Assuming a Flutter version will behave exactly like the native one.

## Who this service is for

A company running two native apps that wants one team to maintain both. An owner of an older hybrid app that is slow or hard to update. A startup that built a first version quickly on another framework and now wants a stable base for growth.

## What we need from you

Access to the current source code as a collaborator, your API documentation, design files if you have them and a description of your users and data. For store updates, we need a developer or team role in your Apple and Google accounts. We never ask for passwords. Before we begin, we send the migration plan for your approval.
